phase_name: Certify a temporally constrained frame and run open items 1 and 2

objectives.description: Choose and certify a constrained frame
Record the certificate as a checked predicate
Experiment C1: multi-time/non-convex realizable minimal settlers
Experiment C2: pointwise-compatible settler/co-settler pair with no common history
Re-check soundness/sufficiency and F5.1 validity profile on this frame

approaches_tried.approach: Forbid a.b -> a.c and search for a multi-time realizable minimal settler of A []-> B at windows {0,1} and {0,1,2}
approaches_tried.reason: A and B are both CF-constituent (state-level exact); alt()'s imposition step restricts its search to the antecedent verifier's own domain regardless of the outer candidate settler's domain, so a transition constraint strictly after the anchor cannot recruit a later time into a minimal settler for this antecedent/consequent shape. See F12's precise mechanism paragraph and the named deciding test (a tensed antecedent/consequent).

approaches_tried.approach: First perturbation-certificate test used an out-of-range state id (999999) as the bogus forbidden pair
approaches_tried.reason: an invalid state id is never in `poss`, so the base relation vacuously reports it as 'not related' and the certificate incorrectly PASSED; fixed by instead building the frame's relation WITHOUT the constraint and certifying a claim that the (valid, resolvable) pair IS forbidden, which correctly reports CERTIFICATE FAIL
